source.author: lucan
source.text: Primus ab aequorea percussis cuspide saxis Thessalicus sonipes bellis feralibus omen Exsiluit; primus chalybem fraenosque momordit, Spumavitque novis Lapithae domitoris habenis.
source.text_original: Primus ab aequorea percussis cuspide saxis / Thessalicus sonipes bellis feralibus omen / Exsiluit; primus chalybem fraenosque momordit, / Spumavitque novis Lapithae domitoris habenis.
source.text_english: First from the sea-shore rocks, struck by the spear, the Thessalian horse sprang forth as an omen of the savage wars; first it bit at the steel and the reins, and it foamed beneath the new harness of its Lapithae-tamer.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: oraque Thessalico melior contundere freno vectorem pavidae Castor dum quaereret Helles, passus Amyclaea pinguescere Cyllaron herba.
reuse.text_original: oraque Thessalico melior contundere freno / vectorem pavidae Castor dum quaereret Helles, / passus Amyclaea pinguescere Cyllaron herba.
reuse.text_english: and while Castor, seeking to tame the rider with the Thessalian bridle, allowed Cyllarus to grow sleek on Amyclean grass, so that he might better master the shores of fearful Helle,
